data.name: Antar
data.gender_notes: Antar is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Antar is a noble and brave warrior mentioned in pre-Islamic Arabic poetry. He is renowned for his chivalry and unwavering loyalty towards his beloved, Qais. The name Antar carries the meaning “Noble and brave warrior” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Antar usually hope their child will grow to embody noble and brave warrior and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of unyielding love and loyalty.
data.etymology: Antar belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Noble and brave warrior.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Antar total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_arabic.name: عنتر
in_arabic.long_meaning: عنتر هو اسم علم مذكر من أصل عربي و معناه الشجاع الذي يقدّم في المعارك و المدح ، و يدل على صفات حميدة مثل الشجاعة و الكرم و الإقدام . ورد اسم عنتر في الشعر العربي القديم و هو من الأسماء التي تعطي دلالة على الفخر و العزة .

in_urdu.name: انتر
in_urdu.meaning: شجاع، مقدام، بہادر، و مدح کا مستحق
in_urdu.long_meaning: انتر ایک عربی نام ہے جس کا مطلب ہے شجاع، مقدام، بہادر، اور مدح کا مستحق ۔ یہ نام عربی جڑوں سے ماخوذ ہے اور اسلامی ثقافت میں اس کی تاریخی اہمیت ہے ۔ جنوبی ایشیائی مسلمانوں میں یہ نام روایتی اور مقبول ہے ۔

in_hindi.name: अंतर
in_hindi.long_meaning: अंतर एक अरबी नाम है जिसका अर्थ है शूरवीर, आगे बढ़ने वाला, वीर और प्रशंसा का पात्र । यह नाम अरबी मूल से लिया गया है और इस्लामी परंपरा में इसका ऐतिहासिक महत्व है । भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में यह नाम पारंपरिक और लोकप्रिय है ।

in_pashto.name: انټر
in_pashto.long_meaning: انټر د عربي اصل يو نوم دی چې مانا يې ده منډک، زړور، ځوښ او د ستاين شایسته . دا نوم د افغاني او پښتني کلتور برخه ده او د تاريخي پلوه د پښتنو د شجاعت او مردانگي سمبول دی .

in_english.name: Antar
in_english.meaning: Brave, courageous, one who advances in battles
in_english.long_meaning: Antar is a masculine given name of Arabic origin, meaning brave, courageous, and one who advances in battles . It is derived from the Arabic root ' -n-t-r' which connotes bravery, chivalry, and heroism . The name has historical significance in Islamic tradition, reflecting attributes of valor and nobility . In various Muslim cultures, Antar symbolizes strength, courage, and honor .

historical_references.reference: Antar ibn Shaddad is a legendary hero and poet from pre-Islamic Arabia. He is considered the greatest hero of the pre-Islamic Arabian poetic tradition. The story of Antar is a tale of love, fidelity, and chivalry. According to legend, Antar was a Bedouin prince and warrior who lived in the Hejaz during the pre-Islamic period. After being banished from his tribe for falling in love with his cousin, Antar embarked on a series of adventures, including battles against enemies and a journey to India to seek the wisdom of the sage al-Harith ibn Kalada.
historical_references.context: Legendary hero from pre-Islamic Arabia, known for his tales of love, fidelity, and chivalry.

historical_references.reference: Antar ibn Al-Harith was a prominent Sufi shaykh who lived during the 11th and 12th centuries. He is most famous for his spiritual teachings and his role as a mentor to the poet Ibn al-Farid. Antar was born in Egypt and studied under various Sufi teachers before settling in Damascus, where he founded a Sufi order called the 'Order of Antar'. His teachings emphasized the importance of detachment, humility, and the love of God.
historical_references.context: Prominent Sufi shaykh, known for his spiritual teachings and role as a mentor to the poet Ibn al-Farid.

modern_usage.modern_context: Antar is a popular figure in Arabic literature and Islamic history, best known for his role in the eponymous pre-Islamic epic poem 'Antar and Abla'. The tale revolves around Antar's unwavering love for Abla, his wife, and their adventures. In modern times, Antar's story continues to resonate with audiences through various platforms. On Goodreads, there are multiple editions of translations of the original Arabic text available for readers. Wikipedia maintains a comprehensive page on Antar, detailing his life, background, and significance in Arabic literature and Islamic history. Lastly, on YouTube, there are numerous videos featuring storytellers retelling the Antar and Abla tale in both Arabic and English, ensuring that Antar's legend lives on.
